"""
Pydantic models and level helpers for the application-log explorer.

Every parsed application-log line travels through this module, so the contract
shared with the ``/api/logs/explorer/*`` endpoints (and therefore with the
Logs Explorer UI) lives in :class:`LogEntry`.

Diagram:
--------
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    raw[raw log line] --> parser[logs/parsers.py]
    parser --> entry[LogEntry]
    entry --> query[logs/query.py]
    query --> api[/api/logs/explorer/query/]
```
"""

from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

#: Canonical level names, most severe first. The index is the severity rank:
#: clients sort and colour the entries from this single ordering.
LEVEL_ORDER = [
    "critical",
    "error",
    "warn",
    "info",
    "debug",
    "trace",
    "unknown",
]

#: ``level -> severity rank`` map built from :data:`LEVEL_ORDER`.
LEVEL_RANK = {level: index for index, level in enumerate(LEVEL_ORDER)}

#: Raw level names found in the wild mapped to the canonical ones.
_LEVEL_ALIASES = {
    "critical": "critical",
    "crit": "critical",
    "fatal": "critical",
    "panic": "critical",
    "error": "error",
    "err": "error",
    "exception": "error",
    "warning": "warn",
    "warn": "warn",
    "info": "info",
    "information": "info",
    "notice": "info",
    "debug": "debug",
    "trace": "trace",
    "verbose": "trace",
}


def normalize_level(level: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """
    Map a raw log level onto one of the canonical values in :data:`LEVEL_ORDER`.

    ``CRITICAL``/``FATAL`` become ``critical``, ``ERROR``/``EXCEPTION`` become
    ``error``, ``WARNING``/``WARN`` become ``warn``, ``INFO``/``DEBUG``/``TRACE``
    are kept, and anything else (including empty input) becomes ``unknown``.

    Args:
        level: Raw level name as found in a log line or a JSON log record.

    Returns:
        One of the values in :data:`LEVEL_ORDER`.
    """
    if not level:
        return "unknown"
    key = str(level).strip().lower().strip("[]():'\"")
    if not key:
        return "unknown"
    return _LEVEL_ALIASES.get(key, "unknown")


class LogLevel:
    """
    Namespace for the canonical level names.

    Kept as a class so callers can write ``LogLevel.ERROR`` instead of a raw
    string while :func:`normalize_level` stays a plain function.
    """

    CRITICAL = "critical"
    ERROR = "error"
    WARN = "warn"
    INFO = "info"
    DEBUG = "debug"
    TRACE = "trace"
    UNKNOWN = "unknown"

    #: Severity ordering, most severe first.
    ORDER = LEVEL_ORDER

    @staticmethod
    def normalize(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
        """Alias of :func:`normalize_level`."""
        return normalize_level(value)

    @staticmethod
    def rank(value: Optional[str]) -> int:
        """Return the severity rank of *value* (``unknown`` when unrecognised)."""
        return LEVEL_RANK.get(normalize_level(value), LEVEL_RANK["unknown"])


class LogEntry(BaseModel):
    """
    A single parsed application-log entry.

    An entry owns its main line plus every continuation line that belonged to
    it (tracebacks, wrapped messages). ``id`` is synthetic but stable, so the
    detail/context endpoints can resolve an entry without an index.

    Attributes:
        id:               ``<source>#<line index>`` — stable per file position.
        timestamp:        Raw timestamp as printed in the log header (``""`` if none).
        ts_ms:            ``timestamp`` in epoch milliseconds (UTC-naive treated
                          as UTC), or ``None`` when it cannot be parsed.
        level:            Canonical level, see :func:`normalize_level`.
        logger:           Logger name from the ``[logger:line]`` header (``""`` if none).
        module:           Module/logger part of the header (``None`` if none).
        line:             Source line number from the header (``None`` if none).
        message:          Message body, continuation lines joined with ``\\n``.
        fields:           Structured extras (``request``, ``profiler``, JSON keys, …).
        continuation_lines: How many lines were appended to ``message``.
        source:           Logical source id the entry was read from (file name).
        raw:              Verbatim text of the entry (main + continuation lines).
    """

    id: str = Field(description="Stable synthetic id: '<source>#<line index>'.")
    timestamp: str = Field(default="", description="Timestamp as printed in the log.")
    ts_ms: Optional[int] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Timestamp in epoch milliseconds (UTC), None when unparsable.",
    )
    level: str = Field(default="unknown", description="Canonical level name.")
    logger: str = Field(default="", description="Logger name from the header.")
    module: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Module from the header.")
    line: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, description="Source line number.")
    message: str = Field(default="", description="Message body with continuations.")
    fields: Dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Structured extras extracted from the entry.",
    )
    continuation_lines: int = Field(
        default=0,
        description="Number of lines appended to the message.",
    )
    source: str = Field(default="", description="Source id (log file name).")
    raw: str = Field(default="", description="Verbatim text of the entry.")

"""
Streaming-friendly parser for application log files.

This is a generalisation of :mod:`codx.junior.log_parser`: the header format,
the continuation-line handling and the request/profiler extractors are the
same ones, but an entry is produced as a :class:`~codx.junior.logs.models.LogEntry`
with a stable id, a normalised level, a parsed timestamp and JSON-logger
support. The extractors are imported from the legacy module (never duplicated),
so ``log_parser.parse_logs`` keeps working for any caller that still uses it.

Primary line format::

    [2026-01-02 10:11:12,345] INFO [logger.name:42] message goes here

Diagram:
--------
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    lines[lines iterable] --> header{header?}
    header -- yes --> new[new entry]
    header -- no --> json{json record?}
    json -- yes --> jsonEntry[json entry]
    json -- no --> cont{continuation?}
    cont -- yes --> append[append to previous entry]
    cont -- no --> unknown[unknown entry]
    new --> extract[request/profiler extractors]
    jsonEntry --> extract
    append --> extract
    unknown --> extract
```
"""

import json
import logging
import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Optional

from codx.junior.log_parser import EXTRACTORS
from codx.junior.logs.models import LogEntry, normalize_level

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: ``[timestamp] LEVEL [logger:line] message`` — the line number and the logger
#: are both optional, the logger may contain dots.
HEADER_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^\[(?P<timestamp>[^\]]+)\]\s+"
    r"(?P<level>[A-Za-z]+)\s+"
    r"\[(?P<logger>[^\[\]:]*)(?::(?P<line>\d+))?\]"
    r"\s?(?P<message>.*)$"
)

#: Prefixes of a line that must be appended to the previous entry, even when
#: the previous entry has no logger (free-form block at the top of a file).
_CONTINUATION_HINTS = (
    "Traceback (most recent call last)",
    "During handling of the above exception",
    "The above exception was the direct cause",
    "Caused by:",
    'File "',
    "Stack trace:",
    "... ",
)

#: Keys that make a JSON line a structured log record.
_JSON_MARKER_KEYS = ("level", "levelname", "severity", "message", "msg", "timestamp", "time")

#: JSON keys consumed by the entry itself (everything else goes to ``fields``).
_JSON_CORE_KEYS = {
    "level",
    "levelname",
    "severity",
    "logger",
    "name",
    "message",
    "msg",
    "timestamp",
    "time",
    "ts",
}

#: ``strptime`` formats accepted for the header/JSON timestamp.
_TS_FORMATS = (
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S",
)


def parse_timestamp_ms(timestamp: Optional[str]) -> Optional[int]:
    """
    Convert a log timestamp to epoch milliseconds.

    Naive timestamps are interpreted as UTC (log files usually carry no zone
    and the explorer only needs a consistent ordering). ISO-8601 values with an
    explicit offset or a trailing ``Z`` are supported as well as bare epoch
    seconds/milliseconds.

    Args:
        timestamp: Timestamp string as printed in the log.

    Returns:
        Epoch milliseconds, or ``None`` when the value cannot be parsed.
    """
    if not timestamp:
        return None
    text = str(timestamp).strip()
    if not text:
        return None

    # Bare epoch values: 13 digits (or more) are milliseconds, 10 are seconds.
    if text.isdigit():
        if len(text) >= 13:
            return int(text)
        if len(text) == 10:
            return int(text) * 1000
        return None

    iso_text = text.replace("Z", "+0000")
    for candidate in (text, iso_text):
        for fmt in _TS_FORMATS:
            try:
                parsed = datetime.strptime(candidate, fmt)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
            if parsed.tzinfo is None:
                parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return int(parsed.timestamp() * 1000)

    # datetime.fromisoformat covers offsets written as "+00:00".
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        logger.debug("parse_timestamp_ms: cannot parse timestamp %r", timestamp)
        return None
    if parsed.tzinfo is None:
        parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return int(parsed.timestamp() * 1000)


def _as_text(value: Any) -> str:
    """Return *value* as text (``""`` for ``None``), JSON-encoding containers."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, (int, float, bool)):
        return str(value)
    try:
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return str(value)


def parse_json_record(line: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Parse *line* as a JSON log record.

    Args:
        line: A single raw log line.

    Returns:
        The decoded dict when the whole line is a JSON object that looks like a
        log record (it carries at least one of ``level``/``message``/``msg``/
        ``timestamp``), otherwise ``None``.
    """
    text = line.strip()
    if not text.startswith("{") or not text.endswith("}"):
        return None
    try:
        record = json.loads(text)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return None
    if not any(key in record for key in _JSON_MARKER_KEYS):
        return None
    return record


class _EntryBuilder:
    """Mutable accumulator for the entry that is currently being read."""

    __slots__ = (
        "columns",
        "continuation_lines",
        "fields",
        "message_parts",
        "offset",
        "raw_parts",
        "source",
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        source: str,
        offset: int,
        timestamp: str = "",
        level: str = "unknown",
        logger_name: str = "",
        module: Optional[str] = None,
        line: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.source = source
        self.offset = offset
        self.columns = {
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "level": level,
            "logger": logger_name,
            "module": module,
            "line": line,
        }
        self.message_parts: List[str] = []
        self.raw_parts: List[str] = []
        self.continuation_lines = 0
        self.fields: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    # ── Content ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def append_message(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Append the first (header) line of the entry."""
        self.message_parts.append(text)

    def append_raw(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Append a raw line exactly as read from the file."""
        self.raw_parts.append(text)

    def add_continuation(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Attach a continuation line (traceback, wrapped message, …)."""
        self.message_parts.append(text)
        self.raw_parts.append(text)
        self.continuation_lines += 1

    @property
    def logger_name(self) -> str:
        """Logger name of the entry (``""`` when the header had none)."""
        return self.columns["logger"]

    # ── Result ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def build(self) -> LogEntry:
        """Materialise the accumulated entry, running the shared extractors."""
        message = "\n".join(self.message_parts)
        raw = "\n".join(self.raw_parts)
        fields: Dict[str, Any] = dict(self.fields)

        for extractor in EXTRACTORS:
            try:
                data = extractor(message)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - extractors must never break parsing
                logger.debug("%s extractor failed: %s", getattr(extractor, "__name__", extractor), exc)
                data = None
            if data:
                fields.update(data)

        timestamp = self.columns["timestamp"] or ""
        return LogEntry(
            id=f"{self.source}#{self.offset}",
            timestamp=timestamp,
            ts_ms=parse_timestamp_ms(timestamp),
            level=self.columns["level"] or "unknown",
            logger=self.columns["logger"] or "",
            module=self.columns["module"],
            line=self.columns["line"],
            message=message,
            fields=fields,
            continuation_lines=self.continuation_lines,
            source=self.source,
            raw=raw,
        )


def _build_json_entry(
    record: Dict[str, Any],
    source: str,
    offset: int,
    raw_line: str,
) -> LogEntry:
    """Build an entry from a structured (JSON logger) record."""
    timestamp = _as_text(
        record.get("timestamp") or record.get("time") or record.get("ts") or ""
    )
    level = normalize_level(
        _as_text(record.get("level") or record.get("levelname") or record.get("severity"))
    )
    logger_name = _as_text(record.get("logger") or record.get("name") or "")
    if not logger_name:
        module_candidate = record.get("module")
        if isinstance(module_candidate, str):
            logger_name = module_candidate
    message = _as_text(record.get("message") or record.get("msg") or "")

    module = record.get("module")
    module = module if isinstance(module, str) and module else None
    line = record.get("line")
    line = line if isinstance(line, int) and not isinstance(line, bool) else None

    fields = {key: value for key, value in record.items() if key not in _JSON_CORE_KEYS}

    return LogEntry(
        id=f"{source}#{offset}",
        timestamp=timestamp,
        ts_ms=parse_timestamp_ms(timestamp),
        level=level,
        logger=logger_name,
        module=module,
        line=line,
        message=message,
        fields=fields,
        continuation_lines=0,
        source=source,
        raw=raw_line,
    )


def _is_continuation(line: str, current: Optional[_EntryBuilder]) -> bool:
    """
    Decide whether *line* continues the entry held by *current*.

    Indented lines always continue. A headerless entry (free-form text at the
    top of a file, ``level='unknown'``) only absorbs traceback-shaped lines so
    that a block of unrelated lines does not collapse into one huge entry.
    """
    if current is None:
        return False
    if line[:1] in (" ", "\t"):
        return True
    stripped = line.strip()
    for hint in _CONTINUATION_HINTS:
        if stripped.startswith(hint):
            return True
    if not current.logger_name:
        return False
    return True


def iter_entries(
    lines: Iterable[str],
    source: str,
    start_index: int = 0,
) -> Iterator[LogEntry]:
    """
    Yield :class:`LogEntry` objects as the lines are consumed.

    Only one entry is held in memory at a time, so this is the entry point for
    huge files: pass an open file object or any line iterator and stop early
    when enough entries were collected.

    Args:
        lines:       Iterable of raw lines (without trailing newlines preferred).
        source:      Logical source id, used to build stable ids.
        start_index: Line index of the first line (for tailing a growing file).

    Yields:
        One :class:`LogEntry` per header line (plus headerless/JSON entries).
    """
    current: Optional[_EntryBuilder] = None

    for offset, raw_line in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")
        if not line.strip():
            # Blank lines carry no information; skipping them keeps messages tidy.
            continue
        index = start_index + offset

        header = HEADER_PATTERN.match(line)
        if header:
            if current is not None:
                yield current.build()
            logger_name = (header.group("logger") or "").strip()
            raw_number = header.group("line")
            current = _EntryBuilder(
                source=source,
                offset=index,
                timestamp=header.group("timestamp").strip(),
                level=normalize_level(header.group("level")),
                logger_name=logger_name,
                module=logger_name or None,
                line=int(raw_number) if raw_number else None,
            )
            current.append_message(header.group("message"))
            current.append_raw(line)
            continue

        record = parse_json_record(line)
        if record is not None:
            if current is not None:
                yield current.build()
                current = None
            yield _build_json_entry(record, source, index, line)
            continue

        if _is_continuation(line, current):
            current.add_continuation(line)
            continue

        if current is not None:
            yield current.build()
        current = _EntryBuilder(source=source, offset=index, level="unknown", logger_name="")
        current.append_message(line)
        current.append_raw(line)

    if current is not None:
        yield current.build()


def parse_lines(
    lines: Iterable[str],
    source: str,
    start_index: int = 0,
) -> List[LogEntry]:
    """
    Parse an iterable of log lines into a list of entries.

    Thin wrapper around :func:`iter_entries` used by the callers that need the
    whole slice (for example a bounded page of a file).

    Args:
        lines:       Iterable of raw lines.
        source:      Logical source id, used to build stable ids.
        start_index: Line index of the first line.

    Returns:
        The parsed entries, in file order.
    """
    return list(iter_entries(lines, source=source, start_index=start_index))

"""
Loki/Graylog-style query language for the application-log explorer.

The language is deliberately small: every whitespace-separated term is
AND-joined and may be negated with a leading ``-``.

=====================  ======================================================
Term                   Meaning
=====================  ======================================================
``error``              case-insensitive substring on the entry raw text
``"exact phrase"``     case-insensitive substring on the entry raw text
``level=error,warn``   level set membership (levels are normalised)
``logger~"chat_.*"``   case-insensitive regex against the logger name
``field=value``        exact match on ``fields[field]`` or a top-level attribute
``field~"regex"``      regex match on ``fields[field]`` or a top-level attribute
``-<term>``            negates any of the terms above
=====================  ======================================================

A regex that does not compile never raises: a warning is logged, the term is
flagged with its error and it degrades to a case-insensitive substring match.

Diagram:
--------
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    q[query text] --> tokenizer
    tokenizer --> terms
    terms --> predicates
    predicates --> LogQuery
    LogQuery -->|matches| entry[LogEntry]
```
"""

import logging
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.logs.models import normalize_level

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Term kinds reported back to the UI.
KIND_TEXT = "text"
KIND_PHRASE = "phrase"
KIND_LEVEL = "level"
KIND_EXACT = "exact"
KIND_REGEX = "regex"

#: Attributes that can be addressed directly with ``name=value``.
TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS = (
    "id",
    "timestamp",
    "ts_ms",
    "level",
    "logger",
    "module",
    "line",
    "message",
    "source",
    "raw",
)

_FIELD_TERM = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<field>[A-Za-z_][\w.\-]*)\s*(?P<op>=|~)\s*(?P<value>.+)$",
    re.DOTALL,
)

Predicate = Callable[[Any], bool]


@dataclass
class QueryTerm:
    """
    A single compiled query term.

    Exposed so the UI can render the parsed query (chips, level filter, …).

    Attributes:
        raw:     The term exactly as written (including the ``-`` and quotes).
        kind:    One of ``text``, ``phrase``, ``level``, ``exact``, ``regex``.
        negated: Whether the term was prefixed with ``-``.
        field:   Field name for ``field=value`` / ``field~regex`` terms.
        value:   Raw value (comma list for level terms).
        values:  Normalised level names for level terms.
        error:   Regex compile error, when the term fell back to a substring.
    """

    raw: str
    kind: str
    negated: bool = False
    field: Optional[str] = None
    value: str = ""
    values: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    error: Optional[str] = None

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON-friendly representation (used by the API/UI)."""
        return {
            "raw": self.raw,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "negated": self.negated,
            "field": self.field,
            "value": self.value,
            "values": list(self.values),
            "error": self.error,
        }


def tokenize(query: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Split a query into terms, keeping quoted sections (with their quotes) whole.

    Args:
        query: Raw query text.

    Returns:
        The terms in the order they were written.
    """
    tokens: List[str] = []
    current: List[str] = []
    in_quotes = False
    escaped = False

    for char in query or "":
        if escaped:
            current.append(char)
            escaped = False
            continue
        if char == "\\" and in_quotes:
            current.append(char)
            escaped = True
            continue
        if char == '"':
            in_quotes = not in_quotes
            current.append(char)
            continue
        if char.isspace() and not in_quotes:
            if current:
                tokens.append("".join(current))
                current = []
            continue
        current.append(char)

    if current:
        tokens.append("".join(current))
    return tokens


def _unquote(value: str) -> str:
    """Strip the surrounding quotes (if any) and unescape ``\\"``."""
    text = value.strip()
    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == '"' and text[-1] == '"':
        text = text[1:-1]
    return text.replace('\\"', '"')


def _lookup(entry: Any, name: str) -> Any:
    """Read *name* from a :class:`LogEntry` (or a plain dict)."""
    if isinstance(entry, dict):
        fields = entry.get("fields")
        if isinstance(fields, dict) and name in fields:
            return fields[name]
        return entry.get(name)
    fields = getattr(entry, "fields", None)
    if isinstance(fields, dict) and name in fields:
        return fields[name]
    return getattr(entry, name, None)


def _entry_level(entry: Any) -> str:
    """Return the canonical level of *entry*."""
    return normalize_level(_lookup(entry, "level"))


def _entry_raw(entry: Any) -> str:
    """Return the searchable raw text of *entry*."""
    raw = _lookup(entry, "raw")
    if raw:
        return str(raw)
    message = _lookup(entry, "message")
    return str(message or "")


def _as_strings(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """Flatten a field value into the strings it can be matched against."""
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set)):
        return [str(item) for item in value if item is not None]
    return [str(value)]


def _text_matcher(needle: str) -> Predicate:
    """Case-insensitive substring match on the entry raw text."""
    wanted = needle.casefold()

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return wanted in _entry_raw(entry).casefold()

    return _match


def _substring_field_matcher(name: Optional[str], needle: str) -> Predicate:
    """Case-insensitive substring match on a field (raw text when no field)."""
    if not name:
        return _text_matcher(needle)
    wanted = needle.casefold()

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return any(wanted in candidate.casefold() for candidate in _as_strings(_lookup(entry, name)))

    return _match


def _exact_matcher(name: str, wanted: str) -> Predicate:
    """Exact (case-insensitive) match on a field or a top-level attribute."""
    target = wanted.casefold()

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return any(candidate.casefold() == target for candidate in _as_strings(_lookup(entry, name)))

    return _match


def _regex_matcher(name: str, pattern: "re.Pattern[str]") -> Predicate:
    """Regex search on a field or a top-level attribute."""

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return any(pattern.search(candidate) for candidate in _as_strings(_lookup(entry, name)))

    return _match


def _level_matcher(levels: List[str]) -> Predicate:
    """Membership of the canonical levels in *levels*."""
    wanted = set(levels)

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return _entry_level(entry) in wanted

    return _match


def _negate(predicate: Predicate) -> Predicate:
    """Invert a predicate (for terms prefixed with ``-``)."""

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return not predicate(entry)

    return _match


def _compile_term(token: str) -> Optional[Any]:
    """
    Compile one query token.

    Args:
        token: A token produced by :func:`tokenize`.

    Returns:
        ``(QueryTerm, predicate)`` or ``None`` for an empty token.
    """
    raw = token
    negated = raw.startswith("-") and len(raw) > 1
    body = raw[1:] if negated else raw
    if not body:
        return None

    # Quoted phrase: "exact phrase"
    if body.startswith('"') and body.endswith('"') and len(body) >= 2:
        value = _unquote(body)
        term = QueryTerm(raw=raw, kind=KIND_PHRASE, negated=negated, value=value)
        predicate: Optional[Predicate] = _text_matcher(value) if value else None
        return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)

    match = _FIELD_TERM.match(body)
    if match:
        name = match.group("field")
        operator = match.group("op")
        value = _unquote(match.group("value"))

        if operator == "=" and name.lower() in ("level", "levels"):
            levels = [normalize_level(part.strip()) for part in value.split(",") if part.strip()]
            term = QueryTerm(
                raw=raw,
                kind=KIND_LEVEL,
                negated=negated,
                field="level",
                value=value,
                values=levels,
            )
            predicate = _level_matcher(levels) if levels else None
            return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)

        if operator == "=":
            term = QueryTerm(
                raw=raw,
                kind=KIND_EXACT,
                negated=negated,
                field=name,
                value=value,
            )
            predicate = _exact_matcher(name, value) if value else None
            return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)

        # operator == "~"
        term = QueryTerm(raw=raw, kind=KIND_REGEX, negated=negated, field=name, value=value)
        if not value:
            return term, None
        try:
            predicate = _regex_matcher(name, re.compile(value, re.IGNORECASE))
        except re.error as exc:
            logger.warning("compile_query: invalid regex %r (%s), using substring", value, exc)
            term.error = str(exc)
            predicate = _substring_field_matcher(name, value)
        return term, (_negate(predicate) if negated else predicate)

    # Bare word / free text
    value = _unquote(body)
    term = QueryTerm(raw=raw, kind=KIND_TEXT, negated=negated, value=value)
    predicate = _text_matcher(value) if value else None
    return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)


class LogQuery:
    """
    A compiled log query: the original text, its terms and the predicates.

    Attributes:
        text:  The query exactly as the user typed it (echoed back to the UI).
        terms: The parsed :class:`QueryTerm` objects, in order.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        text: str = "",
        terms: Optional[List[QueryTerm]] = None,
        predicates: Optional[List[Predicate]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.text = text or ""
        self.terms: List[QueryTerm] = list(terms or [])
        self._predicates: List[Predicate] = list(predicates or [])

    @property
    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` when the query has no effective term (matches everything)."""
        return not self._predicates

    def matches(self, entry: Any) -> bool:
        """
        Return ``True`` when *entry* satisfies every term.

        Args:
            entry: A :class:`~codx.junior.logs.models.LogEntry` or a dict with
                   the same keys (``level``, ``raw``, ``fields``, …).
        """
        return all(predicate(entry) for predicate in self._predicates)

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return not self.is_empty

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug helper
        return f"LogQuery(text={self.text!r}, terms={len(self.terms)})"

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON-friendly representation (echoed by the API)."""
        return {
            "text": self.text,
            "is_empty": self.is_empty,
            "terms": [term.to_dict() for term in self.terms],
        }


def compile_query(query: Optional[str]) -> LogQuery:
    """
    Compile a Loki/Graylog-style query string.

    Args:
        query: Query text, e.g. ``'level=error,warn logger~"chat_.*" -timeout'``.

    Returns:
        A :class:`LogQuery`; an empty or blank query matches every entry.
    """
    text = query or ""
    terms: List[QueryTerm] = []
    predicates: List[Predicate] = []

    for token in tokenize(text):
        compiled = _compile_term(token)
        if compiled is None:
            continue
        term, predicate = compiled
        terms.append(term)
        if predicate is not None:
            predicates.append(predicate)

"""
Tests for the generalised application-log parser.

Pure logic only: no FastAPI, no file system, no log writer involved.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from itertools import islice

import pytest

from codx.junior.logs.models import LEVEL_ORDER, LogEntry, LogLevel, normalize_level
from codx.junior.logs.parsers import (
    HEADER_PATTERN,
    iter_entries,
    parse_json_record,
    parse_lines,
    parse_timestamp_ms,
)


def _ms(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, micro=0):
    """Epoch milliseconds for a UTC-naive log timestamp."""
    return int(datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, micro, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)


def _sample_lines():
    return [
        "[2026-01-02 10:11:12,345] INFO [codx.junior.chat:42] Chat started",
        "[2026-01-02 10:11:13.500] WARNING [codx.junior.db] Slow query",
        'Traceback (most recent call last):',
        '  File "app.py", line 10, in <module>',
        '    raise RuntimeError("boom")',
        "RuntimeError: boom",
        '[2026-01-02 10:11:15] ERROR [codx.junior.api:7] '
        'Request https://example.test/api - 12.3 ms "POST /api/chat HTTP/1.1" 500',
    ]


# ── Header parsing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_header_with_millis():
    entries = parse_lines(
        ["[2026-01-02 10:11:12,345] INFO [codx.junior.chat:42] Chat started"],
        source="api.log",
    )

    assert len(entries) == 1
    entry = entries[0]
    assert isinstance(entry, LogEntry)
    assert entry.id == "api.log#0"
    assert entry.timestamp == "2026-01-02 10:11:12,345"
    assert entry.ts_ms == _ms(2026, 1, 2, 10, 11, 12, 345000)
    assert entry.level == "info"
    assert entry.logger == "codx.junior.chat"
    assert entry.module == "codx.junior.chat"
    assert entry.line == 42
    assert entry.message == "Chat started"
    assert entry.continuation_lines == 0
    assert entry.source == "api.log"
    assert entry.raw == "[2026-01-02 10:11:12,345] INFO [codx.junior.chat:42] Chat started"


def test_header_without_millis_and_without_line_number():
    entries = parse_lines(
        ["[2026-01-02 10:11:12] DEBUG [codx.junior.cache] cache warmed"],
        source="api.log",
    )

    entry = entries[0]
    assert entry.ts_ms == _ms(2026, 1, 2, 10, 11, 12)
    assert entry.level == "debug"
    assert entry.logger == "codx.junior.cache"
    assert entry.line is None
    assert entry.message == "cache warmed"


def test_header_with_empty_logger():
    entries = parse_lines(["[2026-01-02 10:11:12] INFO [:12] anonymous"], source="api.log")

    entry = entries[0]
    assert entry.logger == ""
    assert entry.module is None
    assert entry.line == 12
    assert entry.message == "anonymous"


def test_header_pattern_accepts_dotted_logger_and_iso_like_timestamp():
    match = HEADER_PATTERN.match("[2026-01-02T10:11:12Z] INFO [pkg.sub.mod:12] hello world")

    assert match is not None
    assert match.group("timestamp") == "2026-01-02T10:11:12Z"
    assert match.group("logger") == "pkg.sub.mod"
    assert match.group("line") == "12"
    assert match.group("message") == "hello world"


# ── Continuations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_multiline_traceback_attaches_to_previous_entry():
    entries = parse_lines(_sample_lines(), source="api.log")

    assert [entry.id for entry in entries] == ["api.log#0", "api.log#1", "api.log#6"]
    warning = entries[1]
    assert warning.level == "warn"
    assert warning.continuation_lines == 3
    assert warning.message.splitlines()[0] == "Slow query"
    assert "Traceback (most recent call last):" in warning.message
    assert "RuntimeError: boom" in warning.message
    assert warning.raw.endswith("RuntimeError: boom")
    assert entries[2].message.startswith("Request https://example.test/api")


def test_headerless_lines_become_unknown_entries():
    entries = parse_lines(["plain line one", "plain line two"], source="api.log")

    assert len(entries) == 2
    assert [entry.id for entry in entries] == ["api.log#0", "api.log#1"]
    assert all(entry.level == "unknown" for entry in entries)
    assert all(entry.logger == "" for entry in entries)
    assert all(entry.ts_ms is None for entry in entries)
    assert entries[0].message == "plain line one"


def test_indented_line_continues_a_headerless_entry():
    entries = parse_lines(["plain line", "    indented detail"], source="api.log")

    assert len(entries) == 1
    assert entries[0].level == "unknown"
    assert entries[0].continuation_lines == 1
    assert entries[0].message == "plain line\n    indented detail"


def test_blank_lines_are_skipped_and_do_not_count_as_continuations():
    lines = [
        "[2026-01-02 10:11:12] INFO [a.b:1] first",
        "",
        "   ",
        "  continuation",
    ]

    entries = parse_lines(lines, source="api.log")

    assert len(entries) == 1
    assert entries[0].continuation_lines == 1
    assert entries[0].message == "first\n  continuation"


# ── JSON lines ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_json_line_is_parsed_into_structured_fields():
    payload = {
        "timestamp": "2026-01-02T10:11:12.345Z",
        "level": "ERROR",
        "logger": "uvicorn.error",
        "message": "connection lost",
        "request_id": "req-1",
        "attempt": 2,
    }

    entries = parse_lines([json.dumps(payload)], source="app.jsonl")

    entry = entries[0]
    assert entry.level == "error"
    assert entry.logger == "uvicorn.error"
    assert entry.message == "connection lost"
    assert entry.ts_ms == _ms(2026, 1, 2, 10, 11, 12, 345000)
    assert entry.line is None
    assert entry.fields["request_id"] == "req-1"
    assert entry.fields["attempt"] == 2
    assert "level" not in entry.fields


def test_json_line_accepts_msg_key_and_epoch_millis():
    payload = {"ts": "1767348672000", "level": "warn", "msg": "slow", "module": "api.routes"}
    entry = parse_lines([json.dumps(payload)], source="app.jsonl")[0]

    assert entry.message == "slow"
    assert entry.level == "warn"
    assert entry.logger == "api.routes"
    assert entry.ts_ms == 1767348672000


def test_json_without_log_keys_is_not_a_json_entry():
    line = json.dumps({"foo": 1})

    assert parse_json_record(line) is None
    entry = parse_lines([line], source="api.log")[0]
    assert entry.level == "unknown"
    assert entry.message == line


# ── Extractors shared with codx.junior.log_parser ───────────────────────────


def test_request_extraction():
    line = (
        "[2026-01-02 10:11:15] INFO [codx.junior.api:9] "
        'Request https://example.test/api - 12.3 ms "POST /api/chat HTTP/1.1" 500'
    )

    entry = parse_lines([line], source="api.log")[0]

    assert entry.fields["request"] == {
        "url": "https://example.test/api",
        "status_code": "500",
        "time_taken": 12.3,
        "method": "POST",
    }


def test_profiler_extraction():
    line = '[2026-01-02 10:11:15] INFO [codx.junior.profiler:3] Profiler: {"total": 1.5, "calls": 2}'

    entry = parse_lines([line], source="api.log")[0]

    assert entry.fields["profiler"] == {"total": 1.5, "calls": 2}


def test_invalid_profiler_json_is_ignored():
    line = '[2026-01-02 10:11:15] INFO [codx.junior.profiler:3] Profiler: {"total": '

    entry = parse_lines([line], source="api.log")[0]

    assert "profiler" not in entry.fields


def test_extractors_see_continuation_lines():
    lines = [
        "[2026-01-02 10:11:15] INFO [codx.junior.api:9] Request https://example.test/api - 5.0 ms",
        '  "POST /api/chat HTTP/1.1" 201',
    ]

    entry = parse_lines(lines, source="api.log")[0]

    assert entry.continuation_lines == 1
    assert entry.fields["request"]["status_code"] == "201"


# ── Levels ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "raw,expected",
    [
        ("CRITICAL", "critical"),
        ("fatal", "critical"),
        ("ERROR", "error"),

        ("", "unknown"),

def test_normalize_level(raw, expected):

def test_level_order_and_rank():
    assert LEVEL_ORDER[0] == "critical"
    assert LEVEL_ORDER[-1] == "unknown"
    assert LogLevel.ORDER == LEVEL_ORDER
    assert LogLevel.normalize("FATAL") == "critical"
    assert LogLevel.rank("fatal") == 0
    assert LogLevel.rank("info") < LogLevel.rank("debug") < LogLevel.rank("unknown")


def test_parser_normalises_header_levels():
    entries = parse_lines(

            "[2026-01-02 10:11:12] FATAL [a.b:1] boom",
            "[2026-01-02 10:11:13] EXCEPTION [a.b:2] kaboom",
            "[2026-01-02 10:11:14] WARN [a.b:3] careful",
        ],
        source="api.log",

    assert [entry.level for entry in entries] == ["critical", "error", "warn"]


# ── Ids, timestamps, streaming ──────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_ids_are_unique_and_stable():
    lines = _sample_lines()

    first = parse_lines(lines, source="api.log")
    second = parse_lines(lines, source="api.log")

    assert [entry.id for entry in first] == [entry.id for entry in second]
    assert len({entry.id for entry in first}) == len(first)

def test_start_index_shifts_ids():

def test_iter_entries_is_lazy():

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "timestamp,expected",
    [
        ("2026-01-02 10:11:12,345", _ms(2026, 1, 2, 10, 11, 12, 345000)),
        ("2026-01-02 10:11:12.345", _ms(2026, 1, 2, 10, 11, 12, 345000)),

)

    assert entry.timestamp == "n/a"
    assert entry.ts_ms is None

    assert parse_lines([], source="api.log") == []

"""
Streaming-friendly parser for application log files.

This is a generalisation of :mod:`codx.junior.log_parser`: the header format,
the continuation-line handling and the request/profiler extractors are the
same ones, but an entry is produced as a :class:`~codx.junior.logs.models.LogEntry`
with a stable id, a normalised level, a parsed timestamp and JSON-logger
support. The extractors are imported from the legacy module (never duplicated),
so ``log_parser.parse_logs`` keeps working for any caller that still uses it.

Primary line format::

    [2026-01-02 10:11:12,345] INFO [logger.name:42] message goes here

Diagram:
--------
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    lines[lines iterable] --> header{header?}
    header -- yes --> new[new entry]
    header -- no --> json{json record?}
    json -- yes --> jsonEntry[json entry]
    json -- no --> cont{continuation?}
    cont -- yes --> append[append to previous entry]
    cont -- no --> unknown[unknown entry]
    new --> extract[request/profiler extractors]
    jsonEntry --> extract
    append --> extract
    unknown --> extract
```
"""

import json
import logging
import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Optional

from codx.junior.log_parser import EXTRACTORS
from codx.junior.logs.models import LogEntry, normalize_level

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: ``[timestamp] LEVEL [logger:line] message`` — the line number and the logger
#: are both optional, the logger may contain dots.
HEADER_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^\[(?P<timestamp>[^\]]+)\]\s+"
    r"(?P<level>[A-Za-z]+)\s+"
    r"\[(?P<logger>[^\[\]:]*)(?::(?P<line>\d+))?\]"
    r"\s?(?P<message>.*)$"
)

#: Prefixes of a line that must be appended to the previous entry, even when
#: the previous entry has no logger (free-form block at the top of a file).
_CONTINUATION_HINTS = (
    "Traceback (most recent call last)",
    "During handling of the above exception",
    "The above exception was the direct cause",
    "Caused by:",
    'File "',
    "Stack trace:",
    "... ",
)

#: Keys that make a JSON line a structured log record.
_JSON_MARKER_KEYS = ("level", "levelname", "severity", "message", "msg", "timestamp", "time")

#: JSON keys consumed by the entry itself (everything else goes to ``fields``).
_JSON_CORE_KEYS = {
    "level",
    "levelname",
    "severity",
    "logger",
    "name",
    "message",
    "msg",
    "timestamp",
    "time",
    "ts",
}

#: ``strptime`` formats accepted for the header/JSON timestamp.
_TS_FORMATS = (
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S%z",
    "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S",
)


def parse_timestamp_ms(timestamp: Optional[str]) -> Optional[int]:
    """
    Convert a log timestamp to epoch milliseconds.

    Naive timestamps are interpreted as UTC (log files usually carry no zone
    and the explorer only needs a consistent ordering). ISO-8601 values with an
    explicit offset or a trailing ``Z`` are supported as well as bare epoch
    seconds/milliseconds.

    Args:
        timestamp: Timestamp string as printed in the log.

    Returns:
        Epoch milliseconds, or ``None`` when the value cannot be parsed.
    """
    if not timestamp:
        return None
    text = str(timestamp).strip()
    if not text:
        return None

    # Bare epoch values: 13 digits (or more) are milliseconds, 10 are seconds.
    if text.isdigit():
        if len(text) >= 13:
            return int(text)
        if len(text) == 10:
            return int(text) * 1000
        return None

    iso_text = text.replace("Z", "+0000")
    for candidate in (text, iso_text):
        for fmt in _TS_FORMATS:
            try:
                parsed = datetime.strptime(candidate, fmt)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
            if parsed.tzinfo is None:
                parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            return int(parsed.timestamp() * 1000)

    # datetime.fromisoformat covers offsets written as "+00:00".
    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        logger.debug("parse_timestamp_ms: cannot parse timestamp %r", timestamp)
        return None
    if parsed.tzinfo is None:
        parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return int(parsed.timestamp() * 1000)


def _as_text(value: Any) -> str:
    """Return *value* as text (``""`` for ``None``), JSON-encoding containers."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, (int, float, bool)):
        return str(value)
    try:
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return str(value)


def parse_json_record(line: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Parse *line* as a JSON log record.

    Args:
        line: A single raw log line.

    Returns:
        The decoded dict when the whole line is a JSON object that looks like a
        log record (it carries at least one of ``level``/``message``/``msg``/
        ``timestamp``), otherwise ``None``.
    """
    text = line.strip()
    if not text.startswith("{") or not text.endswith("}"):
        return None
    try:
        record = json.loads(text)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return None
    if not any(key in record for key in _JSON_MARKER_KEYS):
        return None
    return record


class _EntryBuilder:
    """Mutable accumulator for the entry that is currently being read."""

    __slots__ = (
        "columns",
        "continuation_lines",
        "fields",
        "message_parts",
        "offset",
        "raw_parts",
        "source",
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        source: str,
        offset: int,
        timestamp: str = "",
        level: str = "unknown",
        logger_name: str = "",
        module: Optional[str] = None,
        line: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.source = source
        self.offset = offset
        self.columns = {
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "level": level,
            "logger": logger_name,
            "module": module,
            "line": line,
        }
        self.message_parts: List[str] = []
        self.raw_parts: List[str] = []
        self.continuation_lines = 0
        self.fields: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    # ── Content ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def append_message(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Append the first (header) line of the entry."""
        self.message_parts.append(text)

    def append_raw(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Append a raw line exactly as read from the file."""
        self.raw_parts.append(text)

    def add_continuation(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Attach a continuation line (traceback, wrapped message, …)."""
        self.message_parts.append(text)
        self.raw_parts.append(text)
        self.continuation_lines += 1

    @property
    def logger_name(self) -> str:
        """Logger name of the entry (``""`` when the header had none)."""
        return self.columns["logger"]

    # ── Result ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def build(self) -> LogEntry:
        """Materialise the accumulated entry, running the shared extractors."""
        message = "\n".join(self.message_parts)
        raw = "\n".join(self.raw_parts)
        fields: Dict[str, Any] = dict(self.fields)

        for extractor in EXTRACTORS:
            try:
                data = extractor(message)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - extractors must never break parsing
                logger.debug("%s extractor failed: %s", getattr(extractor, "__name__", extractor), exc)
                data = None
            if data:
                fields.update(data)

        timestamp = self.columns["timestamp"] or ""
        return LogEntry(
            id=f"{self.source}#{self.offset}",
            timestamp=timestamp,
            ts_ms=parse_timestamp_ms(timestamp),
            level=self.columns["level"] or "unknown",
            logger=self.columns["logger"] or "",
            module=self.columns["module"],
            line=self.columns["line"],
            message=message,
            fields=fields,
            continuation_lines=self.continuation_lines,
            source=self.source,
            raw=raw,
        )


def _build_json_entry(
    record: Dict[str, Any],
    source: str,
    offset: int,
    raw_line: str,
) -> LogEntry:
    """Build an entry from a structured (JSON logger) record."""
    timestamp = _as_text(
        record.get("timestamp") or record.get("time") or record.get("ts") or ""
    )
    level = normalize_level(
        _as_text(record.get("level") or record.get("levelname") or record.get("severity"))
    )
    logger_name = _as_text(record.get("logger") or record.get("name") or "")
    if not logger_name:
        module_candidate = record.get("module")
        if isinstance(module_candidate, str):
            logger_name = module_candidate
    message = _as_text(record.get("message") or record.get("msg") or "")

    module = record.get("module")
    module = module if isinstance(module, str) and module else None
    line = record.get("line")
    line = line if isinstance(line, int) and not isinstance(line, bool) else None

    fields = {key: value for key, value in record.items() if key not in _JSON_CORE_KEYS}

    return LogEntry(
        id=f"{source}#{offset}",
        timestamp=timestamp,
        ts_ms=parse_timestamp_ms(timestamp),
        level=level,
        logger=logger_name,
        module=module,
        line=line,
        message=message,
        fields=fields,
        continuation_lines=0,
        source=source,
        raw=raw_line,
    )


def _is_continuation(line: str, current: Optional[_EntryBuilder]) -> bool:
    """
    Decide whether *line* continues the entry held by *current*.

    Indented lines always continue. A headerless entry (free-form text at the
    top of a file, ``level='unknown'``) only absorbs traceback-shaped lines so
    that a block of unrelated lines does not collapse into one huge entry.
    """
    if current is None:
        return False
    if line[:1] in (" ", "\t"):
        return True
    stripped = line.strip()
    for hint in _CONTINUATION_HINTS:
        if stripped.startswith(hint):
            return True
    if not current.logger_name:
        return False
    return True


def iter_entries(
    lines: Iterable[str],
    source: str,
    start_index: int = 0,
) -> Iterator[LogEntry]:
    """
    Yield :class:`LogEntry` objects as the lines are consumed.

    Only one entry is held in memory at a time, so this is the entry point for
    huge files: pass an open file object or any line iterator and stop early
    when enough entries were collected.

    Args:
        lines:       Iterable of raw lines (without trailing newlines preferred).
        source:      Logical source id, used to build stable ids.
        start_index: Line index of the first line (for tailing a growing file).

    Yields:
        One :class:`LogEntry` per header line (plus headerless/JSON entries).
    """
    current: Optional[_EntryBuilder] = None

    for offset, raw_line in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")
        if not line.strip():
            # Blank lines carry no information; skipping them keeps messages tidy.
            continue
        index = start_index + offset

        header = HEADER_PATTERN.match(line)
        if header:
            if current is not None:
                yield current.build()
            logger_name = (header.group("logger") or "").strip()
            raw_number = header.group("line")
            current = _EntryBuilder(
                source=source,
                offset=index,
                timestamp=header.group("timestamp").strip(),
                level=normalize_level(header.group("level")),
                logger_name=logger_name,
                module=logger_name or None,
                line=int(raw_number) if raw_number else None,
            )
            current.append_message(header.group("message"))
            current.append_raw(line)
            continue

        record = parse_json_record(line)
        if record is not None:
            if current is not None:
                yield current.build()
                current = None
            yield _build_json_entry(record, source, index, line)
            continue

        if _is_continuation(line, current):
            current.add_continuation(line)
            continue

        if current is not None:
            yield current.build()
        current = _EntryBuilder(source=source, offset=index, level="unknown", logger_name="")
        current.append_message(line)
        current.append_raw(line)

    if current is not None:
        yield current.build()


def parse_lines(
    lines: Iterable[str],
    source: str,
    start_index: int = 0,
) -> List[LogEntry]:
    """
    Parse an iterable of log lines into a list of entries.

    Thin wrapper around :func:`iter_entries` used by the callers that need the
    whole slice (for example a bounded page of a file).

    Args:
        lines:       Iterable of raw lines.
        source:      Logical source id, used to build stable ids.
        start_index: Line index of the first line.

    Returns:
        The parsed entries, in file order.
    """
    return list(iter_entries(lines, source=source, start_index=start_index))

class LogQuery:

    Attributes:

        terms: The parsed :class:`QueryTerm` objects, in order.

    def __init__(
        self,

        terms: Optional[List[QueryTerm]] = None,
        predicates: Optional[List[Predicate]] = None,

        self.text = text or ""
        self.terms: List[QueryTerm] = list(terms or [])
        self._predicates: List[Predicate] = list(predicates or [])

        """``True`` when the query has no effective term (matches everything)."""
        return not self._predicates

    def matches(self, entry: Any) -> bool:
        """
        Return ``True`` when *entry* satisfies every term.

        Args:
            entry: A :class:`~codx.junior.logs.models.LogEntry` or a dict with
                   the same keys (``level``, ``raw``, ``fields``, …).
        """
        return all(predicate(entry) for predicate in self._predicates)

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return not self.is_empty

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug helper
        return f"LogQuery(text={self.text!r}, terms={len(self.terms)})"

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON-friendly representation (echoed by the API)."""
        return {
            "text": self.text,
            "is_empty": self.is_empty,
            "terms": [term.to_dict() for term in self.terms],
        }


def compile_query(query: Optional[str]) -> LogQuery:
    """
    Compile a Loki/Graylog-style query string.

    Args:

    Returns:
        A :class:`LogQuery`; an empty or blank query matches every entry.
    """
    text = query or ""
    terms: List[QueryTerm] = []
    predicates: List[Predicate] = []

    for token in tokenize(text):
        compiled = _compile_term(token)
        if compiled is None:
            continue
        term, predicate = compiled
        terms.append(term)
        if predicate is not None:
            predicates.append(predicate)

    return LogQuery(text=text, terms=terms, predicates=predicates)

"""
Loki/Graylog-style query language for the application-log explorer.

The language is deliberately small: every whitespace-separated term is
AND-joined and may be negated with a leading ``-``.

=====================  ======================================================
Term                   Meaning
=====================  ======================================================
``error``              case-insensitive substring on the entry raw text
``"exact phrase"``     case-insensitive substring on the entry raw text
``level=error,warn``   level set membership (levels are normalised)
``logger~"chat_.*"``   case-insensitive regex against the logger name
``field=value``        exact match on ``fields[field]`` or a top-level attribute
``field~"regex"``      regex match on ``fields[field]`` or a top-level attribute
``-<term>``            negates any of the terms above
=====================  ======================================================

A regex that does not compile never raises: a warning is logged, the term is
flagged with its error and it degrades to a case-insensitive substring match.

Diagram:
--------
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    q[query text] --> tokenizer
    tokenizer --> terms
    terms --> predicates
    predicates --> LogQuery
    LogQuery -->|matches| entry[LogEntry]
```
"""

import dataclasses
import logging
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.logs.models import normalize_level

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Term kinds reported back to the UI.
KIND_TEXT = "text"
KIND_PHRASE = "phrase"
KIND_LEVEL = "level"
KIND_EXACT = "exact"
KIND_REGEX = "regex"

#: Attributes that can be addressed directly with ``name=value``.
TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS = (
    "id",
    "timestamp",
    "ts_ms",
    "level",
    "logger",
    "module",
    "line",
    "message",
    "source",
    "raw",
)

_FIELD_TERM = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<field>[A-Za-z_][\w.\-]*)\s*(?P<op>=|~)\s*(?P<value>.+)$",
    re.DOTALL,
)

Predicate = Callable[[Any], bool]


@dataclass
class QueryTerm:
    """
    A single compiled query term.

    Exposed so the UI can render the parsed query (chips, level filter, …).

    Attributes:
        raw:     The term exactly as written (including the ``-`` and quotes).
        kind:    One of ``text``, ``phrase``, ``level``, ``exact``, ``regex``.
        negated: Whether the term was prefixed with ``-``.
        field:   Field name for ``field=value`` / ``field~regex`` terms.
        value:   Raw value (comma list for level terms).
        values:  Normalised level names for level terms.
        error:   Regex compile error, when the term fell back to a substring.
    """

    raw: str
    kind: str
    negated: bool = False
    field: Optional[str] = None
    value: str = ""
    values: List[str] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)
    error: Optional[str] = None

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON-friendly representation (used by the API/UI)."""
        return {
            "raw": self.raw,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "negated": self.negated,
            "field": self.field,
            "value": self.value,
            "values": list(self.values),
            "error": self.error,
        }


def tokenize(query: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Split a query into terms, keeping quoted sections (with their quotes) whole.

    Args:
        query: Raw query text.

    Returns:
        The terms in the order they were written.
    """
    tokens: List[str] = []
    current: List[str] = []
    in_quotes = False
    escaped = False

    for char in query or "":
        if escaped:
            current.append(char)
            escaped = False
            continue
        if char == "\\" and in_quotes:
            current.append(char)
            escaped = True
            continue
        if char == '"':
            in_quotes = not in_quotes
            current.append(char)
            continue
        if char.isspace() and not in_quotes:
            if current:
                tokens.append("".join(current))
                current = []
            continue
        current.append(char)

    if current:
        tokens.append("".join(current))
    return tokens


def _unquote(value: str) -> str:
    """Strip the surrounding quotes (if any) and unescape ``\\"``."""
    text = value.strip()
    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == '"' and text[-1] == '"':
        text = text[1:-1]
    return text.replace('\\"', '"')


def _lookup_simple(entry: Any, name: str) -> Any:
    """Read a single (non-nested) name from a :class:`LogEntry` or a dict."""
    if isinstance(entry, dict):
        fields = entry.get("fields")
        if isinstance(fields, dict) and name in fields:
            return fields[name]
        return entry.get(name)
    fields = getattr(entry, "fields", None)
    if isinstance(fields, dict) and name in fields:
        return fields[name]
    return getattr(entry, name, None)


def _lookup(entry: Any, name: str) -> Any:
    """
    Read *name* from a :class:`LogEntry` (or a plain dict).

    Structured fields win over attributes, and dotted names (
    ``request.url``) descend into nested dicts.
    """
    value = _lookup_simple(entry, name)
    if value is not None or "." not in name:
        return value

    first, *rest = name.split(".")
    current = _lookup_simple(entry, first)
    for part in rest:
        if isinstance(current, dict):
            current = current.get(part)
        else:
            current = getattr(current, part, None)
        if current is None:
            return None
    return current


def _entry_level(entry: Any) -> str:
    """Return the canonical level of *entry*."""
    return normalize_level(_lookup(entry, "level"))


def _entry_raw(entry: Any) -> str:
    """Return the searchable raw text of *entry*."""
    raw = _lookup(entry, "raw")
    if raw:
        return str(raw)
    message = _lookup(entry, "message")
    return str(message or "")


def _as_strings(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """Flatten a field value into the strings it can be matched against."""
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set)):
        return [str(item) for item in value if item is not None]
    return [str(value)]


def _text_matcher(needle: str) -> Predicate:
    """Case-insensitive substring match on the entry raw text."""
    wanted = needle.casefold()

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return wanted in _entry_raw(entry).casefold()

    return _match


def _substring_field_matcher(name: Optional[str], needle: str) -> Predicate:
    """Case-insensitive substring match on a field (raw text when no field)."""
    if not name:
        return _text_matcher(needle)
    wanted = needle.casefold()

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return any(wanted in candidate.casefold() for candidate in _as_strings(_lookup(entry, name)))

    return _match


def _exact_matcher(name: str, wanted: str) -> Predicate:
    """Exact (case-insensitive) match on a field or a top-level attribute."""
    target = wanted.casefold()

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return any(candidate.casefold() == target for candidate in _as_strings(_lookup(entry, name)))

    return _match


def _regex_matcher(name: str, pattern: "re.Pattern[str]") -> Predicate:
    """Regex search on a field or a top-level attribute."""

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return any(pattern.search(candidate) for candidate in _as_strings(_lookup(entry, name)))

    return _match


def _level_matcher(levels: List[str]) -> Predicate:
    """Membership of the canonical levels in *levels*."""
    wanted = set(levels)

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return _entry_level(entry) in wanted

    return _match


def _negate(predicate: Predicate) -> Predicate:
    """Invert a predicate (for terms prefixed with ``-``)."""

    def _match(entry: Any) -> bool:
        return not predicate(entry)

    return _match


def _compile_term(token: str) -> Optional[Any]:
    """
    Compile one query token.

    Args:
        token: A token produced by :func:`tokenize`.

    Returns:
        ``(QueryTerm, predicate)`` or ``None`` for an empty token.
    """
    raw = token
    negated = raw.startswith("-") and len(raw) > 1
    body = raw[1:] if negated else raw
    if not body:
        return None

    # Quoted phrase: "exact phrase"
    if body.startswith('"') and body.endswith('"') and len(body) >= 2:
        value = _unquote(body)
        term = QueryTerm(raw=raw, kind=KIND_PHRASE, negated=negated, value=value)
        predicate: Optional[Predicate] = _text_matcher(value) if value else None
        return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)

    match = _FIELD_TERM.match(body)
    if match:
        name = match.group("field")
        operator = match.group("op")
        value = _unquote(match.group("value"))

        if operator == "=" and name.lower() in ("level", "levels"):
            levels = [normalize_level(part.strip()) for part in value.split(",") if part.strip()]
            term = QueryTerm(
                raw=raw,
                kind=KIND_LEVEL,
                negated=negated,
                field="level",
                value=value,
                values=levels,
            )
            predicate = _level_matcher(levels) if levels else None
            return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)

        if operator == "=":
            term = QueryTerm(
                raw=raw,
                kind=KIND_EXACT,
                negated=negated,
                field=name,
                value=value,
            )
            predicate = _exact_matcher(name, value) if value else None
            return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)

        # operator == "~"
        term = QueryTerm(raw=raw, kind=KIND_REGEX, negated=negated, field=name, value=value)
        if not value:
            return term, None
        try:
            predicate = _regex_matcher(name, re.compile(value, re.IGNORECASE))
        except re.error as exc:
            logger.warning("compile_query: invalid regex %r (%s), using substring", value, exc)
            term.error = str(exc)
            predicate = _substring_field_matcher(name, value)
        return term, (_negate(predicate) if negated else predicate)

    # Bare word / free text
    value = _unquote(body)
    term = QueryTerm(raw=raw, kind=KIND_TEXT, negated=negated, value=value)
    predicate = _text_matcher(value) if value else None
    return term, (_negate(predicate) if predicate and negated else predicate)


class LogQuery:
    """
    A compiled log query: the original text, its terms and the predicates.

    Attributes:
        text:  The query exactly as the user typed it (echoed back to the UI).
        terms: The parsed :class:`QueryTerm` objects, in order.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        text: str = "",
        terms: Optional[List[QueryTerm]] = None,
        predicates: Optional[List[Predicate]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.text = text or ""
        self.terms: List[QueryTerm] = list(terms or [])
        self._predicates: List[Predicate] = list(predicates or [])

    @property
    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` when the query has no effective term (matches everything)."""
        return not self._predicates

    def matches(self, entry: Any) -> bool:
        """
        Return ``True`` when *entry* satisfies every term.

        Args:
            entry: A :class:`~codx.junior.logs.models.LogEntry` or a dict with
                   the same keys (``level``, ``raw``, ``fields``, …).
        """
        return all(predicate(entry) for predicate in self._predicates)

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return not self.is_empty

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug helper
        return f"LogQuery(text={self.text!r}, terms={len(self.terms)})"

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON-friendly representation (echoed by the API)."""
        return {
            "text": self.text,
            "is_empty": self.is_empty,
            "terms": [term.to_dict() for term in self.terms],
        }


def compile_query(query: Optional[str]) -> LogQuery:
    """
    Compile a Loki/Graylog-style query string.

    Args:
        query: Query text, e.g. ``'level=error,warn logger~"chat_.*" -timeout'``.

    Returns:
        A :class:`LogQuery`; an empty or blank query matches every entry.
    """
    text = query or ""
    terms: List[QueryTerm] = []
    predicates: List[Predicate] = []

    for token in tokenize(text):
        compiled = _compile_term(token)
        if compiled is None:
            continue
        term, predicate = compiled
        terms.append(term)
        if predicate is not None:
            predicates.append(predicate)

    return LogQuery(text=text, terms=terms, predicates=predicates)

"""
Streaming-friendly parser for application log files.

This is a generalisation of :mod:`codx.junior.log_parser`: the header format,
the continuation-line handling and the request/profiler extractors are the
same ones, but an entry is produced as a :class:`~codx.junior.logs.models.LogEntry`
with a stable id, a normalised level, a parsed timestamp and JSON-logger
support. The extractors are imported from the legacy module (never duplicated),
so ``log_parser.parse_logs`` keeps working for any caller that still uses it.

Primary line format::

    [2026-01-02 10:11:12,345] INFO [logger.name:42] message goes here

Diagram:
--------
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    lines[lines iterable] --> header{header?}
    header -- yes --> new[new entry]
    header -- no --> json{json record?}
    json -- yes --> jsonEntry[json entry]
    json -- no --> cont{continuation?}
    cont -- yes --> append[append to previous entry]
    cont -- no --> unknown[unknown entry]
    new --> extract[request/profiler extractors]
    jsonEntry --> extract
    append --> extract
    unknown --> extract
```
"""

import json
import logging
import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Optional

from codx.junior.log_parser import EXTRACTORS
from codx.junior.logs.models import LogEntry, normalize_level

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: ``[timestamp] LEVEL [logger:line] message`` — the line number and the logger
#: are both optional, the logger may contain dots.
HEADER_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^\[(?P<timestamp>[^\]]+)\]\s+"
    r"(?P<level>[A-Za-z]+)\s+"
    r"\[(?P<logger>[^\[\]:]*)(?::(?P<line>\d+))?\]"
    r"\s?(?P<message>.*)$"
)

#: Prefixes of a line that must be appended to the previous entry, even when
#: the previous entry has no logger (free-form block at the top of a file).
_CONTINUATION_HINTS = (
    "Traceback (most recent call last)",
    "During handling of the above exception",
    "The above exception was the direct cause",
    "Caused by:",
    'File "',
    "Stack trace:",
    "... ",
)

#: Keys that make a JSON line a structured log record.
_JSON_MARKER_KEYS = ("level", "levelname", "severity", "message", "msg", "timestamp", "time")

#: JSON keys consumed by the entry itself (everything else goes to ``fields``).
_JSON_CORE_KEYS = {
    "level",
    "levelname",
    "severity",
    "logger",
    "name",
    "message",
    "msg",
    "timestamp",
    "time",
    "ts",
}

#: ``strptime`` formats accepted for the header/JSON timestamp.
_TS_FORMATS = (
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z",
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S%z",
    "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S,%f",
    "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S",
)


def parse_timestamp_ms(timestamp: Optional[str]) -> Optional[int]:
    """
    Convert a log timestamp to epoch milliseconds.

    Naive timestamps are interpreted as UTC (log files usually carry no zone
    and the explorer only needs a consistent ordering). ISO-8601 values with an
    explicit offset or a trailing ``Z`` are supported as well as bare epoch
    seconds/milliseconds.

    Args:
        timestamp: Timestamp string as printed in the log.

    Returns:
        Epoch milliseconds, or ``None`` when the value cannot be parsed.
    """
    if not timestamp:
        return None
    text = str(timestamp).strip()
    if not text:
        return None

    # Bare epoch values: 13 digits (or more) are milliseconds, 10 are seconds.
    if text.isdigit():
        if len(text) >= 13:
            return int(text)
        if len(text) == 10:
            return int(text) * 1000
        return None

    iso_text = text.replace("Z", "+0000")
    for candidate in (text, iso_text):
        for fmt in _TS_FORMATS:
            try:
                parsed = datetime.strptime(candidate, fmt)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
            if parsed.tzinfo is None:
